notes: Run 2026-10-04 01:44 UTC (run 37168826626): selected tasks [8 Performance, 10 Take Repo Forward, 4 Engineering Investments]. Task 8: reviewed DateTimeNano.cs for allocation hotspots; found TryParse(string) allocated up to 9 substrings via Group.Value for int.Parse - switched to Group.ValueSpan + int.Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char>), zero-allocation, same behavior, 90/90 tests pass on net8/9/10. Created draft PR. (Note: attempted a deeper span-based parse avoiding regex Match(string) entirely via EnumerateMatches, but abandoned it - EnumerateMatches doesn't expose named capture groups, so it can't eliminate the ToString() needed for the ISpanParsable path without a full custom parser; reverted that attempt.) Task 4: ran `dotnet list package --outdated`, found protobuf-net.Core (the only runtime dependency) has 3.4.30 available within the same major version - bumped and verified build+tests pass on all 3 TFMs. Test-only packages (NUnit, Test.Sdk, NUnit3TestAdapter, coverlet.collector) have MAJOR version bumps available but were deliberately deferred per project guidelines (prefer minor/patch; only propose major with clear benefit) - logged for future consideration. Task 10: reviewed state of previous 3 open PRs (#40, #41, #42) - all still open/draft/unreviewed with no CI configured and no conflicts, nothing actionable to push; concluded that the most valuable forward progress this run was the two new PRs above rather than touching unreviewed branches. Updated Monthly Activity issue #38 with both new PRs added to Suggested Actions and a new run history entry. Next run: check if any of the 5 open PRs (#40, #41, #42, perf-valuespan, eng-protobuf-bump) were merged or reviewed; if repo accumulates many open repo-assist PRs with no maintainer activity, consider surfacing that explicitly as a suggested action (e.g. batch-review request) rather than continuing to add more. Consider major test-tooling bumps (NUnit 5/Test.Sdk 18/NUnit3TestAdapter 6/coverlet 10) as a bundled Task 4 PR in a future run if a dedicated review window seems warranted.
